transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... see, I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They watch when I leave, and they're slipping notes about me to the front office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just notices on the doors, like regular maintenance stuff or whatever, but I know what's really happening. 

It's just like when I lived over on 4th Street a long time ago. The manager there drove this big blue Ford truck, and he used to park it right by the dumpster just to keep an eye on what I was throwing away. My sister told me I was making a big deal out of nothing back then, too. She used to bake these incredible peach cobblers, though... man, I haven't had a good peach cobbler in probably ten, maybe fifteen years. The peaches you get at the grocery store nowadays, they just don't taste the same, you know? They're all hard and got no real flavor to 'em, like they picked 'em too early. 

But anyway, yeah, the people at my building now, they're definitely watching me and passing those notes to the office.

Do you believe that the people in your apartment building are specifically targeting you or plotting against you, or do you feel like everyday things are happening that have a special meaning for you?

Well, they're definitely targeting me, specifically. It ain't just random everyday stuff. I mean, I know they're watching my comings and goings, keeping a close eye on me, and then slipping those notes about me straight to the office. Everybody keeps trying to tell me, "Oh, it's just regular notices on the doors, they're just taping up water shut-off papers or whatever," but I know what's really going on. 

They hand 'em right to the lady at the front desk. She's got these thick glasses with little fake diamonds in the corners... my Aunt Peggy used to wear glasses just like that. She lived down in Florida, right near the water. Used to collect those big conch shells on the beach. You put 'em up to your ear and it sounds like the ocean, you know? I always wondered how that worked. Somebody told me once it's something about the air bouncing around inside the spiral of the shell, or maybe it's just the blood rushing in your own ear. The human body is real strange like that, the way the ears work. I had an earache real bad when I was a kid... 

But anyway, yeah, they're plotting something with those notes, I'm sure of it, no matter what anybody else says about it being regular building notices.
Have you ever experienced or believed something that others might find extremely strange or not based in reality, even if it feels completely true to you?

Well, I guess... I mean, yeah, like I was saying, it's the whole thing with the people at my apartment. People think it's strange, sure. They keep telling me, "Oh, it's just notices on the doors, they're just taping up maintenance papers," but I know it's not. I know they're watching my comings and goings and slipping notes about me to the office. It feels completely true to me because it *is* true. 

Just like that time I tried to tell my neighbor about the stray cats around the building. There used to be this one orange tabby that would sit right on the hood of my car. Left little muddy paw prints all over the windshield. You try to wash that off and it just smears everywhere, especially if you don't have good wiper fluid. I used to buy the blue kind, but then they started selling that bug-wash stuff that's green. It smells real strong, kinda like ammonia or something. You ever notice how smells can take you right back to a memory? Like how the smell of fresh cut grass always makes me think of high school. I dropped out in the 10th grade, but I used to help the groundskeeper mow the football field before I left. He had this big riding mower... 

But yeah, everybody thinks I'm crazy or whatever about the apartment people, but I know they're watching me and writing those notes.

Do you believe that the people in your apartment building are watching you or plotting against you in ways that you haven't already described, such as following you, eavesdropping on your conversations, or trying to harm you?

Well, I haven't caught 'em following me down the street or anything like that, no. It's mostly just... like I said, I know they're watching my comings and goings right there at the building, and slipping those notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors, but I know better. 

I don't know about eavesdropping, but you can hear right through the walls in that place anyway. The walls are paper thin. You can hear the guy next door watching his television all night. He watches those old black-and-white westerns. I used to love westerns when I was a kid. John Wayne, Clint Eastwood... my dad took me to see a Clint Eastwood movie at the drive-in once. We had this big old station wagon with the wood paneling on the side. You don't see cars like that anymore. Now everything looks like a jellybean, all rounded off and aerodynamic. They say it saves on gas, but gas used to be, what, less than a dollar a gallon back then? We used to drive all the way up to the lake on the weekends... 

But no, I don't think they're trying to physically hurt me or anything. Just watching me leave and come back, and passing those notes to the front office.
Do you feel completely certain that these notes are about you and being passed to the office, even though others have told you they're just regular building notices?

I am absolutely certain. I mean, I know what I see. Everybody keeps saying, "Oh, it's just maintenance papers, it's just notices on the doors," but I know they're watching my comings and goings and slipping notes about me straight to the office. It's the whole reason I even came in here in the first place, because it's just... it's too much. 

It's like how you just know when a storm is coming, you know? You can feel it in your bones. My knees always ache right before it rains. The doctor told me it's barometric pressure changing, something about the fluid in the joints expanding. I used to work construction, roofing mostly, back before my back gave out. Hauling those heavy bundles of shingles up a ladder all day in the hot sun... you'd sweat through your shirt by 9 AM. We used to keep a big orange cooler of ice water in the back of the foreman's truck. Those coolers are great, the ones with the little white button you push to get the water out. Sometimes the button would get stuck, though, and water would just pour everywhere, making a huge mud puddle in the dirt. Mud is terrible to get out of work boots. You gotta let it dry completely and then bang 'em together... 

But yeah, I don't care what anybody else says about those notes. I know they're about me, and I know they're giving them to the office.
Outside of what you've told me about the notes and being watched, do you ever experience other unusual thoughts or beliefs that other people might not understand or agree with?

Well, no, not really. I mean, the main thing is just what I've been saying. I came in here because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings, and they're slipping those notes about me to the office. Even though everybody keeps telling me, "Oh, it's just notices on the doors, it's just regular paperwork," I know what's really happening. 

Paperwork is a hassle anyway, isn't it? I remember when I tried to apply for disability after my back gave out from all that roofing. The stack of forms they sent me in the mail was thicker than a phone book. You remember phone books? The Yellow Pages. They used to just drop them right on your front porch every year. My grandmother used to use an old one as a booster seat for me at the kitchen table when I was real little. She made the best pot roast on Sundays. Cooked it low and slow all day with carrots and potatoes in this heavy cast-iron Dutch oven. Cast iron is great, but you can't ever wash it with soap, or it ruins the seasoning. You just gotta scrub it with coarse salt and a little oil. I bought a cheap pan at the discount store a few years back, non-stick, but the coating started flaking off into my eggs after like two weeks. You gotta be careful with that Teflon stuff, they say it causes all sorts of health problems if you ingest it... 

But anyway, no, I don't really have any other strange thoughts or anything. Just the stuff with the apartment and the notes. That's what's been bothering me.
Have you ever believed something that you know other people don’t believe, even if you can’t explain it to them or they don’t understand it?

I feel like I'm repeating myself here, doc. It's just what I've been telling you. People don't believe me about the apartment, they just keep saying they're regular notices on the doors. But I know they're watching my comings and goings and slipping notes about me to the office. That's the only thing. They leave them right on the door... well, near the door. 

My door actually has this awful draft coming in underneath it, to be honest. The weather stripping is completely shot. I tried to fix it myself with some of that foam tape you get at the hardware store. You ever use that stuff? It comes in a roll, but the adhesive on the back is terrible. It sticks to your fingers better than it sticks to the wood. I ended up with a piece stuck to my thumb for two days. Reminds me of when I used to build model airplanes when I was a teenager. That model glue... man, the smell of that stuff was strong. You'd sit in your bedroom with the door closed trying to glue tiny little landing gear onto a B-17 bomber, and you'd get a headache from the fumes. I had a whole fleet of them hanging from my ceiling on fishing line. My mom hated dusting them. She used this big yellow feather duster, used to knock the propellers right off if she wasn't careful. She was always rushing when she cleaned, always had somewhere to be... 

But yeah, I don't have any other beliefs like that. Just the truth about what's going on at my building, even if nobody else wants to see it.
Have you ever believed something that you know most people would find completely不可思议 or impossible, like something out of a science fiction movie or a fantasy story?

Look, doc, I don't know how many times I can say the same thing. No science fiction, no aliens, no fantasy stories. I'm just a regular guy. The only thing I'm dealing with, the whole reason I even came in here, is because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings, and they're slipping those notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps telling me, "Oh, it's just notices on the doors, it's just regular building stuff," but I know better. 

I mean, speaking of doors, you wouldn't believe the hinges on mine. They squeak like crazy. Squeak, squeak, every time you open it. I tried WD-40, you know, the little can with the red straw? I always lose the straw. It just pops off and rolls under the fridge. Fridges are so heavy to move. Last time I tried to clean behind mine, I found a quarter from 1982. 1982... that was a good year. I had this old Ford pickup truck back then. Two-tone, blue and white. It had a bench seat, the kind where the springs would poke you right in the back if you hit a pothole. Potholes in this city are terrible, aren't they? They just throw some loose gravel in there and call it fixed, and next time it rains, boom, you blow a tire. Tires are so expensive now. 

But yeah, no sci-fi stuff. Just the truth about my apartment and those notes.
Have you ever believed something that you know most people would find completely不可思议 or impossible, like something out of a science fiction movie or a fantasy story?

I really feel like we're just going in circles now, doc. I mean, I'm telling you, there's no crazy science fiction stuff happening. I'm not crazy. I just... I know what I know. I came in here because the people at my apartment building, they're watching my comings and goings. They're keeping tabs on me, and they're slipping these notes about me to the front office. And yeah, everyone I talk to, they just brush it off. They tell me, "Oh, it's just regular notices on the doors, it's just building maintenance," but they don't see what I see. 

Speaking of maintenance, the guy they have working there now, he doesn't know a wrench from a screwdriver. I saw him trying to fix the railing by the stairs last week, and he was using duct tape. Duct tape! I mean, duct tape is great for some things, sure. I used it once to patch a hole in a tent when I went camping up near the lake. That was years ago, back when my back wasn't so bad. We caught a bunch of trout that weekend. Pan-fried them right over the fire with some butter and lemon. You can't beat fresh fish like that. The stuff you buy at the supermarket, it always smells a little off, you know? Like it's been sitting in that display case just a little too long. I try to only buy frozen fish now, the kind that comes in those vacuum-sealed bags. They're hard to open, though. You always need scissors, and my scissors always go missing. I think they get pushed to the back of the junk drawer. Everyone has a junk drawer, right? Mine is full of old batteries and rubber bands. 

But anyway, no, no fantasy stories or impossible things. Just the reality of them watching me at the apartment, even if no one else believes it.
Do you ever believe that certain events, objects, or people have special or hidden meanings that others don't seem to notice or understand?

Doc, I... I feel like a broken record. We're talking about the same thing again. It's not about special hidden meanings in random objects. It's just what I've been saying this whole time. I came in here because I know the people at my apartment building are watching my comings and goings. They're keeping tabs on me, and they're slipping those notes about me to the front office. Everybody keeps telling me, "Oh, it's just regular notices on the doors, they leave them for everyone," but they don't get it. They don't see what's actually happening. 

Speaking of the front office, they have this big bowl of peppermints on the desk. You know the kind, wrapped in that clear plastic that twists at the ends? I took one the other day, and the wrapper was so tight I couldn't get it open. My hands just don't work like they used to. Arthritis, I guess. It's worse when it rains. The humidity just gets right into my knuckles. My granddad used to say he could predict a storm better than the weatherman just by how his knees felt. He was a farmer, out in Ohio. Grew corn, mostly. I remember visiting him when I was a kid, running through the cornfields. The stalks were taller than I was. You could get lost in there so easily. It was like a giant maze. We'd play hide and seek for hours until my grandma would ring this big cast-iron bell on the porch for supper. She made the best fried chicken. Always used a cast-iron skillet. Those skillets are so heavy, though. You drop one of those on your foot, you're going to the hospital for sure. Hospitals always smell like bleach and rubbing alcohol... 

But yeah, no hidden meanings in things. Just the notes they slip to the office about me. That's the only thing going on.

It sticks to your fingers better than it sticks to the wood. I ended up with a piece stuck to my thumb for two days. Reminds me of when I used to build model airplanes when I was a teenager. That model glue... man, the smell of that stuff was strong. You'd sit in your bedroom with the door closed trying to glue tiny little landing gear onto a B-17 bomber, and you'd get a headache from the fumes. I had a whole fleet of them hanging from my ceiling on fishing line. My mom hated dusting them. She used this big yellow feather duster, used to knock the propellers right off if she wasn't careful. She was always rushing when she cleaned, always had somewhere to be... 

But yeah, I don't have any other beliefs like that. Just the truth about what's going on at my building, even if nobody else wants to see it.

I mean, speaking of doors, you wouldn't believe the hinges on mine. They squeak like crazy. Squeak, squeak, every time you open it. I tried WD-40, you know, the little can with the red straw? I always lose the straw. It just pops off and rolls under the fridge. Fridges are so heavy to move. Last time I tried to clean behind mine, I found a quarter from 1982. 1982... that was a good year. I had this old Ford pickup truck back then. Two-tone, blue and white. It had a bench seat, the kind where the springs would poke you right in the back if you hit a pothole. Potholes in this city are terrible, aren't they? They just throw some loose gravel in there and call it fixed, and next time it rains, boom, you blow a tire. Tires are so expensive now. 

But yeah, no sci-fi stuff. Just the truth about my apartment and those notes.

I really feel like we're just going in circles now, doc. I mean, I'm telling you, there's no crazy science fiction stuff happening. I'm not crazy. I just... I know what I know. And yeah, everyone I talk to, they just brush it off. They tell me, "Oh, it's just regular notices on the doors, it's just building maintenance," but they don't see what I see. 

Speaking of maintenance, the guy they have working there now, he doesn't know a wrench from a screwdriver. I saw him trying to fix the railing by the stairs last week, and he was using duct tape. Duct tape! I mean, duct tape is great for some things, sure. I used it once to patch a hole in a tent when I went camping up near the lake. That was years ago, back when my back wasn't so bad. We caught a bunch of trout that weekend. Pan-fried them right over the fire with some butter and lemon. You can't beat fresh fish like that. The stuff you buy at the supermarket, it always smells a little off, you know? Like it's been sitting in that display case just a little too long. I try to only buy frozen fish now, the kind that comes in those vacuum-sealed bags. They're hard to open, though. You always need scissors, and my scissors always go missing. I took one the other day, and the wrapper was so tight I couldn't get it open. My hands just don't work like they used to. Arthritis, I guess. It's worse when it rains. The humidity just gets right into my knuckles. My granddad used to say he could predict a storm better than the weatherman just by how his knees felt. He was a farmer, out in Ohio. Grew corn, mostly. I remember visiting him when I was a kid, running through the cornfields. The stalks were taller than I was. You could get lost in there so easily. It was like a giant maze.
